newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SES SAYS POWERLESS OVER SINGAPORE DUAL LIST LIMITS.
newsitem.headline: SES SAYS POWERLESS OVER SINGAPORE DUAL LIST LIMITS.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) said on Friday it was not responsible for setting or removing limits on companies' foreign shareholdings.
"The imposition of limits on foreign shareholdings in Singapore listed companies are set either by law or by the companies themselves, in view of the nature of their businesses," it said.
"The limits are not set by the SES and it is not for the SES to remove the limits," it added.
The SES was responding to queries from Reuters.
The stock market has been rife this week with speculation that companies with dual listing might merge the local and foreign tranches of their shares listed on the exchange.
The daily Business Times on Friday also published a straw poll among companies with dual listing suggesting that many would prefer any move to abolish the dual listing to come from the authorities.
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said earlier it had no intention of asking banks to merge their local and foreign tranches.
Under Singapore law, foreigners can hold up to 40 percent of bank shares.
